name: Gradlon

attributes.attribute: the only one to escape the flood of Ys
defeated the Vikings on the Loire

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gradlon ruled as king of Brittany in Breton legend. His daughter Dahut governed the sunken city of Ys, whose people turned hard and selfish and drove beggars from their gates. Each night Dahut chose the handsomest visitor and gave him a mask to pass the guard. By dawn the mask squeezed tight and killed him, until the sea drowned the whole city. Only Gradlon escaped, led off by the saint Guénolé, who gave him a horse. The horse refused to carry both, so Gradlon pushed Dahut into the water. The beast then leaped and struck the Rock of Garrec, leaving a hoofprint. Some say Dahut fell into the Abyss of Ahéz. Others say she lives on as a mermaid who lures men. Elsewhere Gradlon appears as the model regional king who enriched Brittany and beat the Vikings on the Loire.

okr.objective: Tell the story of King Gradlon, the sinking of Ys, and his escape from the flood.
key_results: Gradlon ruled Brittany and fathered Dahut.
Dahut's city Ys was drowned when its people grew hard and selfish.
Only Gradlon escaped, led by the saint Guénolé on horseback.
The horse refused to move until Gradlon pushed Dahut into the sea.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2003
